func Cost(books []int) int {

func solve(counts [5]int, memo map[[5]int]int) int {
    // sort descending
    c := [5]int(counts)
    sort.Slice(c[:], func(i, j int) bool { return c[i] > c[j] })
    if c[0] == 0 {
        return 0
    }
    if v, ok := memo[c]; ok {
        return v
    }
    k := 0
    for _, v := range c {
        if v > 0 {
            k++
        }
    }
    best := int(^uint(0) >> 1) // max int
    maxG := k
    if maxG > 5 {
        maxG = 5
    }
    // iterate over all subsets of positions of each size g
    for g := 1; g <= maxG; g++ {
        for mask := 0; mask < 32; mask++ {
            if popcount(mask) != g {
                continue
            }
            nc := c
            for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
                if mask&(1<<i) != 0 {

            sort.Slice(nc[:], func(i, j int) bool { return nc[i] > nc[j] })
            cost := prices[g] + solve(nc, memo)
            if cost < best {
                best = cost
            }
        }
    }
    memo[c] = best
    return best
}

func popcount(x int) int {
    n := 0
    for x > 0 {
        n += x & 1

`book_store.go` now computes the minimum basket cost for the Book Store discount problem from `.docs/instructions.md`.

**Approach:** Count copies per title (5 titles), then run an exact dynamic program over the sorted per-title counts. Because all titles are symmetric, the canonical state is just the counts sorted descending. From each state it tries every valid group size (1–5) and every choice of which titles to take one copy from, memoizing results.
